  FITTED SCALABILITY  speed-up(N) = N / (1 + σ(N-1) + κN(N-1))
    σ (contention, cannot overlap) ... 0.4800
    κ (interference between workers)  0.005290
    residual sum of squares ......... 0.0135
    predicted best worker count ..... 10 (1.7x)

  Paste into config/config.yaml under `orchestrator:` to make the
  estimate the researcher sees reflect this machine:
    scalability_contention: 0.4800
    scalability_coherency: 0.005290

  Shortest wall-clock: 16 workers (70.0s)
  Best per worker-minute: 1 workers (7.99 completions/worker-minute)
  These differ: past the second number, extra workers shorten the
  run by less than they cost. That is the point the governor
  detects at run time and stops growing at.

  A fixture on loopback has no network latency, so the ABSOLUTE times
  say nothing about a real crawl. What is measured faithfully is the
  SHAPE — process startup, database contention, the scheduler and the
  host broker are all the production ones.
